name: Larry Alwin
blurb: Larry Alwin (Democratic, Thermopolis): Independent business-intelligence consultant, working from home. Earlier taught computer classes to adults for about three years, then spent about a decade at a Colorado company that made software for school districts, becoming its director of analytics. He said much of the consulting work had dried up over the past year as artificial intelligence took hold. Lost the Nov. 3, ate Representative H28 with 13.2% of the vote.
occupation: Independent business-intelligence consultant, working from home. Earlier taught computer classes to adults for about three years, then spent about a decade at a Colorado company that made software for school districts, becoming its director of analytics. He said much of the consulting work had dried up over the past year as artificial intelligence took hold.
background: Thermopolis resident (mailing city on the candidate filing) running as a Democrat for House District 28.

Grew up in a ranching family in western Nebraska; he told a 2024 forum he was born in Harris, Nebraska, the middle of five children, just across the Wyoming border on Highway 20. After graduating from Chadron State with a teaching degree he taught computer classes to adults, then moved into software work. He later moved to Thermopolis for his husband’s job.

Also ran for House District 28 in 2024 as a Democrat, after receiving enough write-in votes in the primary to accept the nomination, and lost to incumbent Republican John Winter. He told the Cody Enterprise he received about 20% of the vote in that race.

positions.text: Said people deserve a choice on the ballot and that he was running even though he expected to lose. It was his second campaign for House District 28.

Opposes Proposition 1, saying it would strain county budgets; he said the last round of property-tax cuts forced his county to cut its budget by $2.2 million, reducing funding for programs such as 4-H and the library. Instead he wants tax relief aimed at retirees, including exempting retirees from property taxes.
Opposes Wyoming’s school voucher program and called education “the most important thing in Wyoming.” Opposes selling public lands to private owners: “Keep our public lands in public hands.”
Wants more investment in rural infrastructure such as cell service, saying there is no complete cell service between Thermopolis and Powell.

At an October 2024 Chamber of Commerce forum he supported freedom of choice in health care and expanding Medicaid, and said government should stay out of “bedrooms and our doctor’s offices” while regulating industries that harm people.

name: Jeffrey Haggit
blurb: Jeffrey Haggit (Constitution, Mt View): Recently retired instrumentation technician after 49 years at the same company in southwest Wyoming’s minerals-extraction industry, including trona processing and stack monitoring (self-described, October 2026). Lost the Nov. 3, 2026 general election for U.S. Representative with 4.3% of the vote.
occupation: Recently retired instrumentation technician after 49 years at the same company in southwest Wyoming’s minerals-extraction industry, including trona processing and stack monitoring (self-described, October 2026)
background: Has lived in Wyoming since 1976; mailing city on the candidate filing is Mountain View (Uinta County). Third campaign for U.S. House on the Constitution Party line (also 2020 and 2024). Former chairman of the Constitution Party of Wyoming. Also served on the United Way of Southwest Wyoming’s Uinta Advisory Council, according to Wyoming Public Media.

positions.topic: Federal power and the Tenth Amendment
positions.text: Wants to restrain the federal government and return power to the states under the Tenth Amendment, saying Washington has “got too big for their britches.”

Opposes the current pace of data-center development, citing water and electricity use and concern they could support a surveillance state; says communities should not give tax breaks and that the issue is for states to work out.
Opposes property taxes in principle and supports the 50% residential cut ballot measure, while favoring a Uinta County 1% sales tax for fire apparatus if it offsets lost property-tax revenue.

Supports continuing coal jobs and clean-burn technology from his stack-monitoring work; said the country needs another oil refinery. Opposed foreign military alliances such as those he associated with the NDAA and said the United Nations should be removed from the country.

name: Dave Hardesty
blurb: Dave Hardesty (Independent, Gillette): Teacher and 20-year educator in Wyoming (described as a current teacher in May 2026); U.S. Coast Guard veteran. Lost the Nov. 3, ate Representative H31 with 19.1% of the vote.
occupation: Teacher and 20-year educator in Wyoming (described as a current teacher in May 2026)
background: Gillette resident (mailing city on the candidate filing) running as an Independent for House District 31 against Republican Douglas Moore.

A 20-year educator and Coast Guard veteran and a University of Wyoming graduate. An avid outdoorsman who has camped in every national forest in the state. Previously ran for House District 31 as an independent in 2018 and lost to then-incumbent Republican Scott Clem, 814 votes to 1,826.
education: Graduate of the University of Wyoming

positions.text: Cited the state of public education as a primary reason for running. As a current teacher he said “less government” often means fewer teachers, larger class sizes, and fewer student opportunities, and he advocated that the Legislature financially support public schools as required by the Wyoming Constitution.
Questioned calls for tax cuts and said candidates should specify which programs they intend to terminate.

Voiced concern that abandoning county roads can grant private access to public lands, and said that should be stopped. Proposed codifying corner crossing into law and funding the marking of high-interest crossings. Called for more investment in wildlife crossings on interstates and highways. Said he would work to allow anglers to drop anchor and wade-fish entire rivers where private land lies under navigable waterways.
Said he is running as an independent to evaluate ideas on their own merit rather than follow a national party agenda, with a platform focused on Wyoming’s specific needs.

name: Shawn Johnson
blurb: Shawn Johnson (Libertarian, Thermopolis): Attorney in Wyoming, primarily family law and criminal defense, with some civil litigation; former Natrona County deputy sheriff (about 13 years); Army National Guard combat medic, 21 years: seven years in the Colorado National Guard and the remainder in the Wyoming National Guard; combat deployment to Iraq, 2003–2004. Joined junior year of high school.. Lost the Nov. 3, 2026 general election for U.S. Representative with 7.5% of the vote.
occupation: Attorney in Wyoming, primarily family law and criminal defense, with some civil litigation; former Natrona County deputy sheriff (about 13 years)
background: Born in Casper; spent his teenage years in the Denver area and graduated high school in Westminster, Colorado, then returned to Wyoming. Married, with two stepdaughters and a son; mailing city and current residence Thermopolis (self-reported). Also ran as a Libertarian for House District 28 in 2020.
education: Associate and bachelor’s degrees in business (Army-funded); J.D., Mitchell Hamline School of Law, St. Paul, Minnesota, 2024. Graduated high school in Westminster, Colorado.
military: Army National Guard combat medic, 21 years: seven years in the Colorado National Guard and the remainder in the Wyoming National Guard; combat deployment to Iraq, 2003–2004. Joined junior year of high school.
prior_offices: Casper City Council, 2014–2022; Vice mayor of Casper, 2019–2019; Chair, Libertarian Party of Wyoming (as reported)

positions.text: Wants an independent Wyoming voice who can form coalitions, check executive power, and represent the state rather than follow party or White House direction. As a third-party member he said an evenly split Congress could give Wyoming leverage.

Cited cost of living and an “unnecessary Middle Eastern war” with Iran as linked problems he would want to end; also cited high health-care costs, lost rural-hospital funding after changes to the Affordable Care Act, and the need for a replacement that lowers insurance costs.
Campaign site emphasizes individual liberty, careful use of tax money, and sending Americans into harm’s way only as a last resort.

name: Justin Morgan
blurb: Justin Morgan (Republican, Riverton): Runs a horse-training business in Riverton; U.S. Marine Corps veteran. Lost the Nov. 3, ate Representative H33 with 34.9% of the vote.
occupation: Runs a horse-training business in Riverton
background: Riverton resident (mailing city on the candidate filing). Filed Aug. 27, 2026, as the Republican nominee for House District 33, after the August primary; he did not appear in the ore.

Nominated as a Republican write-in in the Aug. 18, 2026 primary for House District 33 (41 votes, 35.3% of the named write-in total reported on Ballotpedia; there was no named Republican on the primary ballot). Lost the Nov. 3, 2026 general election to incumbent Ivan Posey.

Wyoming native and Marine Corps veteran who ran businesses in North Carolina before moving back in 2004. Has lived in Riverton about 20 years, where he runs a horse-training business. Told a League of Women Voters forum he had not thought about politics until people approached him, and that his children are homeschooled through a program with Riverton High School. His mother was a teacher her whole life. He has two daughters.

positions.text: Supports Proposition 1, the 50% property-tax cut for longtime owners. He said property taxes have gone up 73% since 2019 by his count, and that his research showed the cut would amount to 1.8% of the budget, which governments should be able to adjust.
Opposes Medicaid expansion, saying it would raise taxes on people who are already struggling and that hospitals will see anyone who walks in.

Said last session’s school-funding recalibration needs work and that school-board members he spoke with wanted money earmarked for teacher raises. Supports vouchers for homeschool families but said students on state money should take the same tests as public-school students. Supports full funding for the basket of goods, including art, music, and science.

Opposes selling public land (“I don’t think we should ever sell one square foot of public land”) but would like the state to have more control over it. Supports making corner crossing legal. Not a big supporter of AI data centers; wants companies to pay into an escrow account for cleanup, be taxed at a higher rate, and have no access to water without water rights. Said wind and solar clutter the landscape and kill wildlife, though he could support rooftop solar. On state revenue he said, “Drill baby drill.”

Supports requiring a state ID to vote. Supports secure ballot drop boxes and opposes purging voters from the rolls for skipping a general election. Opposes open primaries and supports replacing voting machines with hand counts.
Said in his closing that he would never vote to defund police, fire, or ambulance services or take away hunting and fishing.

blurb: Joseph Porambo (Libertarian, Casper): Restaurant manager for several decades; in a 2022 interview he also described his work as retail management. Lost the Nov. 3, ate Representative H58 with 10.3% of the vote.
occupation: Restaurant manager for several decades; in a 2022 interview he also described his work as retail management
background: Casper resident (mailing city on the candidate filing) running as a Libertarian for House District 58.

Casper Libertarian who has run repeatedly for office: he announced a 2014 U.S. Senate bid first as an independent, then as a Libertarian (K2 Radio reported he was 54 and a registered Republican at the time); appeared on later general-election rosters as the Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate in 2018 and for House District 58 in 2020; and ran for the Natrona County School District Board of Trustees in 2022.

In a 2022 school-board candidate interview he said he was a grandfather of two children who had recently entered public school, favored allowing willing teachers to be armed after training, wanted more trade-skill options in the curriculum, opposed critical race theory in Natrona schools, and opposed banning two challenged library books from high schools.

name: Carrie Satterwhite
blurb: Carrie Satterwhite (Libertarian, Ralston): Certified instructor for Love and Logic parenting classes through Park County School District 1; also a CASA volunteer in the Fifth Judicial District and a foster grandparent at Westside Elementary in Powell. Lost the Nov. 3, ate Representative H50 with 14.0% of the vote.
occupation: Certified instructor for Love and Logic parenting classes through Park County School District 1; also a CASA volunteer in the Fifth Judicial District and a foster grandparent at Westside Elementary in Powell
background: Ralston resident (mailing city on the candidate filing) running as a Libertarian for House District 50.
Has lived in Ralston more than 40 years. This was her second campaign for House District 50; she ran as a Libertarian in 2022 and lost the general election to incumbent Rachel Rodriguez-Williams.

Leads Love and Logic parenting classes through Park County School District 1 and said she was one test away from national certification as a parenting trainer. For about 10 years she has volunteered as a foster grandparent at Westside Elementary in Powell, recently working mostly with special-education students. She is a CASA volunteer in the Fifth Judicial District, working with abused children and children removed from their homes, and helps transport neighbors to free food giveaways.
education: Left Powell High School without graduating and earned a GED. Later earned a business degree with a minor in accounting, a degree in office administration, and an honors certificate at Northwest College

positions.text: Priorities include health-care access. She said Wyoming has not expanded Medicaid and that many people cannot get care; free clinics cannot handle more complicated needs, and there are not enough treatment beds for mental illness or addiction.

Said shifting the property-tax burden to a higher sales tax or a new state tax would still be a tax. She wants Wyoming to legalize cannabis for medical and recreational use and direct that revenue to property-tax relief and other needs. She said she lobbies lawmakers in Cheyenne every year on the issue.
Said government should focus on core services such as police and fire and stay out of people’s private lives. Other stated priorities include veterans’ benefits and public lands.
Said the state must protect the landscapes and Old West feel that draw visitors while still attracting industry and good-paying jobs. She supports keeping gates closed on backcountry roads.
